language.script_notes: Without the regional co-official languages of the north/east — this is the linguistic 'home' region of standard Spanish.
false_friends: Southern Spain (dry farmland can look similar)

road_furniture.curb_style: Long straight roads across open plateau farmland.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Noticeably long, flat, empty horizon-to-horizon roads.

architecture.wall_construction: Warm-toned stone and stucco farmhouses; grand imperial-era stone architecture and boulevards in Madrid; historic walled towns (Ávila, Toledo, Segovia) with Romanesque/Mudéjar influence.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Warm ochre and tan tones matching the dry plateau landscape; formal grey/cream stone in Madrid's historic core.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Historic walled cities (Ávila's complete medieval walls, Toledo, Segovia's Roman aqueduct); windmills on the La Mancha plain (Don Quixote country); grand formal Madrid architecture and boulevards.

nature.vegetation: Vast dryland wheat and barley fields cover the plateau; sparse scrub and holm oak in less-cultivated stretches; La Mancha's windmill-dotted plains are iconic.
nature.terrain: The high (610-760m), gently undulating Meseta Central plateau dominates, broken by block mountain ranges dividing it into northern (Castile-León) and southern (Castile-La Mancha/Extremadura) basins.
nature.climate_signature: Harsh continental climate — intensely hot dry summers, cold winters; a golden-brown, wide-open, sun-bleached plateau look most of the year.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Higher urban vehicle density in and around Madrid.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 4 in and around Madrid; older/thinner coverage in the sparsely populated rural plateau.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense in Madrid; genuine gaps across the emptier stretches of rural Castile.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Dry farmland, similar hot climate and sparse vegetation in summer
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Central Spain's Meseta is a flatter, higher-elevation plateau with wheat/barley fields and windmill-dotted plains; Andalusia has whitewashed pueblos blancos, olive groves in dense grid rows, and a more Moorish-influenced architectural style.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script/plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Central Spain is dry, flat and golden-brown; Green Spain is wet, hilly, stone-built and green year-round.
